q7.answer: Workers learn of a mode change by reading `billing_mode` from the config service before each charge, and a worker that cannot read it does not charge and raises an alert. I did not decide what happens to an invoice already in flight when a forward move changes the mode; the only in-flight handling I specified is the rollback path (Freeze, then Resolve checks unconfirmed charges by idempotency key), with the per-customer, per-period idempotency key as the backstop against a double charge from a stale read.

q8.answer: The evidence is the nightly per-day gate evidence rows from the comparison job (invoices compared, mismatches, rate), with the decision recorded in the append-only transition log. Nothing lets someone promote early: the move is checked against the gate when a person approves it, and if the gate is not met the move is refused and the mode stays `shadow`.

q9.answer: The brief does not name a component that detects the automatic rollback condition, so I did not decide one. The condition itself is that the new engine's charge failure rate exceeds 2% over any 10-minute window while in `both` or `new_only`, and when it is met the rollback starts automatically at Freeze.

q10.answer: Freeze halts new-engine charge submissions, so no new charges go out from the new engine during the rollback. Due charges are not dropped: queued due charges are handed to the old engine in Resolve, and the old engine makes the charges for the due-and-uncharged set only in ChargeDue, after Freeze, Resolve, Reconcile and CatchUp have finished. If the config service is unavailable, due charges queue rather than being dropped.

q11.answer: Resolve queries the provider by idempotency key for every charge the new engine sent without a confirmed result, so a charge that already succeeded is recognised. Reconcile then places any charge with a ledger entry and a provider success in a 'charged, never charged again' group, and ChargeDue charges only the due-and-uncharged set. The ledger's one-key-per-customer-and-period rule, which both engines send to the provider, blocks a second charge even if a worker reads a stale mode.

q12.answer: Billing stays in RollingBack, and the failed step is retried from the same point and on-call is paged. Each step is idempotent, so a retry is safe, and the rollout can neither move forward nor abort back to `both`. A Freeze step that a worker has not acknowledged stops the rollback from advancing to Resolve, and a failed Verify keeps the rollout in RollingBack until it passes.
